newsitem.title: ITALY: Rome to host Albania conference in late July.
newsitem.headline: Rome to host Albania conference in late July.

text.p: Rome will host a high-level international conference on Albania at the end of July, Italian Foreign Minster Lamberto Dini said on Thursday.
He said Franz Vranitzky, the head of an OSCE mission to Albania, and the Balkan nation's new Socialist leaders would be invited to attend.
"On the Albanian side, we expect representatives of the new Socialist government which we hope will be installed by then," Dini said in a speech to the Senate Foreign Affairs committee.
The ex-Communist Socialist party triumphed in an election held on June 29 and July 6 which were called to end months of anarchy in Albania triggered by the collapse of pyramid saving schemes.
Dini said the conference's aim would be to assess the post-election situation in Albania and to discuss further economic and financial aid.
The summit would also aim to secure a commitment from the country's new leaders to continue the process of national reconciliation, he said.
Italy leads a 7,000-strong international security force in Albania which is expected to withdraw fully by August 12.
